subject: Discovery recap: embeddings & reranking (Borealis Retail)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@borealisretail.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: embeddings & reranking (Borealis Retail)

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed set of next steps so we're aligned. I captured what you said; please correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Reranking latency is a blocker for conversions: p95 currently 300–500ms for a single-query rerank step and spikes during promotions.
- Unit cost is high because each user query fires a dense-retrieval + cross-attention rerank step (we heard 2–3 model calls).
- Index growth: currently ~12M vectors, expecting to grow to ~40–50M over the next 12 months.
- Batch patterns: nightly ingest (bulk) of ~250k–500k items; incremental real-time updates for new SKUs.
- Current stack: Pinecone for vectors, Postgres for metadata, FAISS used for offline experiments.

Success criteria you called out
- Latency: p95 rerank end-to-end under 120ms for typical queries (hybrid retrieval + rerank).
- Throughput: sustain burst to 300 QPS during peak campaigns without degraded p95.
- Cost: reduce per-search inference cost by ~3x vs current spend.
- Quality: measurable NDCG uplift (your internal eval) or match/exceed current relevance at parity latency.

Redwood POC scope (high level)
- 2-week technical POC focused on rerank latencies and cost: we’ll run your sample dataset and replicate production traffic patterns.
- Recommended config: 2 x GPU nodes (A100-class equivalence) with KV cache and prefix caching for popular queries; quantized embedder for cost savings.
- Evaluation: we’ll run an NDCG + latency report, and provide a trace-level cost breakdown (tokens/embeddings/compute).

Immediate next steps
1) You to share a 1–2 week sample of production traffic + a small sample of the catalog (we discussed 100k item sample + 1M query trace or scaled synthetic trace).
2) We’ll send a POC scope + rough cost estimate (attached: redwood-poc-proposal.pdf and cost sheet).
3) Schedule a tech deep-dive next week (30–60m) with Rishi to review infra requirements and security/compliance checklist.

Attachments: redwood-poc-proposal.pdf (POC scope), redwood-cost-estimate.xlsx (ballpark pricing).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Rishi on the deployment options (Dedicated vs Private) once we confirm the dataset.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@borealisretail.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@borealisretail.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 17:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: embeddings & reranking (Borealis Retail)

Thanks Marissa — this looks accurate and helpful. Couple of clarifications from our side:
- Confirming index size: ~12M live vectors today. Expected growth profile: ~2–3x in 6 months, ~4x–5x in 12 months (targeting ~50M).
- Vector DB: currently on Pinecone; we are evaluating Milvus for cost and on-prem potential.
- Embeddings: 1536-d vectors produced by our in-house embedder; considering migration to a smaller dim if it keeps quality.
- Query mix: ~70% similarity search + 30% hybrid rerank; typical rerank window 10–50 candidates.
- Peak QPS: up to ~300 QPS during flash sales, normally 50–80 QPS.

I attached a small export of production metrics that shows traffic and latency patterns (borealis-prod-metrics.csv).

We’re happy to do the POC — please include Camila and Rishi in the technical plan and send any infra/security pre-reqs. Also: can you provide a rough ballpark for a Dedicated POC (2 GPUs) vs hosted POC? A back-of-envelope monthly cost range would be helpful for our finance/ops to greenlight.

I’ll loop in Priya on procurement timelines after we see the POC proposal.

—
Alex Turner
Head of Search & Personalization, Borealis Retail
alex.turner@borealisretail.com | +1 (212) 555-0899

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@borealisretail.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: embeddings & reranking (Borealis Retail)

Appreciate the details, Alex — that helps a lot. A few quick replies to your asks and some proposed timelines:

POC / pricing ballpark
- Hosted POC (Redwood hosted): 2-week POC running on hosted capacity — ballpark $6k–9k depending on traffic replay and storage needs.
- Dedicated trial (reserved nodes): 2 GPUs for a month (trial pricing available for qualifying customers) — rough $12k–18k for the month including infra and monitoring addons. We’ll provide an exact quote in the attached cost spreadsheet.

Technical approach (high level)
- Retrieval layer: keep approximate ANN (Milvus or Pinecone) for candidate generation.
- Rerank: lightweight encoder for most queries and cross-attention rerank as a fallback for top-k where latency allows. We use KV cache + prefix caching to keep identical/repeat queries under p95 targets.
- Quantization: 8-bit/4-bit quantization on the embedder where feasible to cut inference cost without significant quality loss.

POC deliverables and timeline
- Day 0–2: ingest sample dataset (you supply sample CSV) and baseline run.
- Day 3–7: traffic replay and latency/cost profiling.
- Day 8–10: tuning (batching, caching, quantization) and rerun.
- Day 11–14: produce NDCG + latency report and recommended production config.

Attachments: redwood-cost-estimate.xlsx (detailed ballpark), poc-scope.md (detailed runbook).

Next actions (for this week)
1) Alex/Priya: share the sample dataset and a 7–14 day query trace by EOD Friday.
2) Redwood: send calendar invites for technical deep-dive (Rishi + Camila) and deliver the formal POC proposal by Monday.

If you’re good with this, we’ll kick off once the sample dataset is uploaded to the Drive link I shared.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—
Marissa Cole
